name: Glycolysis
summary: Ten enzyme-catalysed steps in the cytosol convert one glucose into two pyruvate. The preparatory phase spends 2 ATP; the payoff phase runs twice (once per triose) and yields 4 ATP and 2 NADH.
net: Glucose + 2 NAD⁺ + 2 ADP + 2 Pᵢ → 2 Pyruvate + 2 NADH + 2 H⁺ + 2 ATP + 2 H₂O

steps.regulation: Muscle hexokinase is inhibited by its product, glucose 6-phosphate. Liver glucokinase (hexokinase IV) has a high Km and is not inhibited by G6P.
steps.note: Phosphorylation traps glucose in the cell: there is no transporter for G6P.
Aldose → ketose isomerisation. It puts a free OH on C-1 for the next phosphorylation and sets up a symmetrical C-3/C-4 cleavage.

steps.regulation: Main control point and committed step. Activated by AMP, ADP and fructose 2,6-bisphosphate. Inhibited by ATP and citrate.
steps.note: From this point on, the sugar is committed to glycolysis.
Class I aldolase works by covalent catalysis through a Schiff base with an active-site lysine (see Unit 12).
Only G3P continues down the pathway, so every later step happens twice per glucose.
Oxidation of the aldehyde is coupled to the uptake of inorganic phosphate, forming a high-energy acyl phosphate.
Substrate-level phosphorylation. In red blood cells, some 1,3-BPG is diverted to 2,3-BPG, the haemoglobin effector from Unit 10.
The phosphoryl group moves from C-3 to C-2, via a 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate intermediate.

steps.regulation: Inhibited by fluoride (with Mg²⁺ and phosphate).
steps.note: Dehydration produces PEP, which has a very high phosphoryl-transfer potential.

steps.regulation: Activated by fructose 1,6-bisphosphate (feed-forward). Inhibited by ATP, acetyl-CoA, alanine and long-chain fatty acids. The liver isoform is also inhibited by phosphorylation (glucagon).
steps.note: The enol → keto tautomerisation of pyruvate makes this step strongly exergonic.

whatIf.q: Blood for glucose measurement is collected into fluoride tubes. Why?
whatIf.a: Fluoride inhibits enolase (step 9), so red and white cells stop consuming glucose in the tube and the measured value stays accurate.

whatIf.q: Arsenate replaces phosphate at step 6. What happens to ATP yield?
whatIf.a: 1-Arseno-3-phosphoglycerate hydrolyses spontaneously, bypassing step 7. Glycolysis continues, but the ATP from step 7 is lost, so the net yield falls to zero.

whatIf.q: A muscle cell's ATP is high and AMP is low. Which step slows down most, and why?
whatIf.a: Step 3: PFK-1 is allosterically inhibited by ATP and needs AMP/ADP for activation, so flux through the committed step drops.
